title: Secretary of State of Ohio

context.text: Incumbent Secretary of State Frank LaRose is term-limited and is running for state auditor. Robert Sprague won the Republican primary over Marcell Strbich with about 70%; Allison Russo won the Democratic primary over Bryan Hambley with about 67%; Tom Pruss was unopposed in the Libertarian primary.
A proposed constitutional amendment (Issue 3) that would put voter-identification requirements, including Ohio's existing in-person photo ID rule, into the state constitution is on the same ballot.

candidates.name: Robert Sprague
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary with about 70% of the vote.

summary.text: Robert Sprague is the Republican nominee. He is the Ohio Treasurer, a former three-term state representative from Findlay and a former Findlay city auditor and treasurer. His campaign emphasizes citizenship checks at registration, photo ID, printed paper ballots, fewer mail-ballot options and making Election Day a state holiday.

background.text: Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from Duke University (1996) and an MBA from the University of North Carolina; worked as a management consultant for Ernst & Young and ran his own consulting firm.
Served as city auditor and treasurer of Findlay, Ohio, then in the Ohio House of Representatives (appointed in 2011, elected to three terms).
Elected Ohio Treasurer in 2018 (53%-47% over Rob Richardson) and took office January 14, 2019.

priorities.text: "My goal in the secretary of state's office is to run fair, transparent, secure elections."
Eliminate ballot drop boxes, require photo ID for mail ballots and verify applicants' citizenship against government records before registering them, as summarized by the USA TODAY Network.
Work with the General Assembly to make Election Day a state holiday.

statements.context: Describing, to the Ohio Capital Journal as reported by the USA TODAY Network, one of the "incremental improvements" he would make to Ohio elections

record.text: As Treasurer, launched ResultsOHIO, a program under which public dollars reimburse project costs only if a project delivers verifiable results.
As Treasurer, oversaw development of the Family Forward adoption-cost loan program (reduced-interest loans up to $50,000) and the STABLE Account program for people with disabilities.

candidates.name: Allison Russo
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with about 67% of the vote.

summary.text: Allison Russo is the Democratic nominee. She is a state representative from Upper Arlington who served as House Minority Leader from January 2022 to 2025 and sat on the Ohio Redistricting Commission. Before office she worked more than 20 years in health policy. Her campaign focuses on protecting ballot access, limiting partisan influence over election administration and opposing the removal of ballot drop boxes.

background.text: Doctorate in health policy from George Washington University, master's degree in epidemiology from the University of Alabama at Birmingham, and bachelor's degree from Mississippi University for Women.
Worked in health policy for more than 20 years before holding office; policy research director at Kennell and Associates since 2010.
First elected to the Ohio House in 2018 and re-elected to four terms; House Minority Leader from 2022 until stepping down in 2025.

priorities.text: Be "an advocate for all voters" and run "fair, free and secure elections."
Prioritize resources for county boards of elections and increase voter engagement, particularly among young people.
Reduce partisan influence in election administration, including how ballot language is written.

record.text: Served on the Ohio Redistricting Commission; largely opposed Republican-drawn congressional and statehouse maps but backed a compromise for state House and Senate districts that is in place through 2030.
Opposed changes to Ohio's voter ID laws and an amendment that would make it harder to amend the Ohio Constitution.

candidates.name: Tom Pruss
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Libertarian primary.

summary.text: Tom Pruss is the Libertarian nominee. He owns a Toledo printing business, has run for the Toledo school board, Lucas County clerk of courts and, in 2024, Ohio's 9th Congressional District, where he received about 4%. He supports voter ID with free state identification, ballot access reform and ranked-choice voting.

background.text: Owner of NorthCoast Print Mail Marketing in Toledo since 2017, in the printing industry since 1985.
Vice president of the Northwest Ohio Polish Cultural Center and former president of the Polish American Community of Toledo.

priorities.text: Protect ballot access: enforce ballot laws equally and oppose unnecessary signature hurdles.
Secure elections without voter suppression: voter ID with free state IDs, transparent voter-roll maintenance and auditable systems.
Reforms such as ranked-choice voting to give voters more choices.

researchNotes: Slate: the Ohio Secretary of State's certified candidate list could not be loaded (403 bot check); the three-candidate slate rests on Ballotpedia and two news reports (Columbus Dispatch, Oct 12, 2026; USA TODAY Network, Sept-Oct 2026). Sprague's campaign website could not be located; his views come from news coverage, so only one short verbatim phrase is shown as a statement. Russo's voting record was not reviewed bill-by-bill (the legislature's website was unreachable); record items are from the Columbus Dispatch. No documentary-proof-of-citizenship stance is stated directly by any candidate in a source reviewed, so no positions were scored.
